question: Should OpenClaw permanently admit exact-ID, already-installed and enabled `workspace-directory` Codex plugins, and own the minimum app-server contract for `marketplaceKinds` plus remote plugin detail IDs?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but it partially reopens a recently restored curated-only boundary and depends on an evolving upstream RPC; only maintainers can authorize those durable product/security and compatibility contracts.

options.title: Approve constrained workspace support
options.body: Accept the exact-ID, no-install, owned-and-accessible app boundary and document the compatible Codex app-server requirement.

options.title: Retain curated-only support
options.body: Reject workspace admission until upstream stabilizes the RPC or maintainers select a different integration boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained workspace support
recommendation.body: Accept the exact-ID, no-install, owned-and-accessible app boundary and document the compatible Codex app-server requirement.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history attributes the canonical native-plugin inventory and thread-policy implementation to this owner, making them the strongest available decision route.
